## Motivation

The alignment-aware staging-size fix in #45394 by @mickqian currently has no focused manager/allocator regression. Raw tensor sizes can fit the default 1 MiB buddy block while the aligned writer rejects the second tensor, and list None entries can fail before writing.

This is a tests-only supplement to #45394. It targets `codex/diffusion-stage-deployment` so the diff contains only the new test file. The implementation remains credited to the original PR; these tests can be merged or cherry-picked into it.

## Modifications

Add one CPU-registered `CustomTestCase` file covering nine staging scenarios: the default 1 MiB boundary, alignment edges at 511/512/513 bytes, a single tensor, a zero-length tail, list holes, absent fields, and all-None lists. Assert real tensor round trips, manifest offsets/list indices, and whole-pool reuse after cleanup.

Only pinned-memory allocation, device-event availability, and the unused transfer-engine boundary are mocked. The actual manager, allocator, writer and reader are imported normally and executed. No staging-size algorithm is copied into the tests.

## Accuracy Tests

Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu:

```bash
SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/sglang-cache PYTHONPATH=python \
  python test/registered/unit/multimodal_gen/test_transfer_staging.py -v
```

- On the #45394 head `ab0c3e671769dc75c18412d6cb05ff54e5a9f959`: 4 test methods covering 9 scenarios pass.
- The same file against main `c8054551012b3df729a0f7c409af95f74286e416` fails in 5 scenarios: 3 existing slot-boundary ValueErrors and 2 None-entry AttributeErrors.
- Repository pre-commit checks on the new file and `git diff --check` pass.

GPU copies/events, RDMA/Mooncake, distributed execution and model-serving accuracy are not validated here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance claim. The tests use at most a 2 MiB CPU pool per scenario, require no model weights, and register with a 5-second CPU CI estimate.

## Checklist

- [x] Run repository pre-commit checks on the new file.
- [x] Add focused CPU regression coverage and verify pre-fix failure.
- [x] Follow repository test placement, CustomTestCase and CI-registration conventions.
- [x] Keep the diff tests-only and credit the existing implementation.
- [ ] Complete upstream review and applicable CI.

AI assistance was used to inspect the public code, develop the regressions and prepare this PR. All reported local checks were actually run.

detail.title: [Test] diffusion/disaggregation: Cover aligned transfer staging

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,130 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""CPU regressions for aligned diffusion transfer staging."""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.disaggregation.transport.buffer import (
+    TransferTensorBuffer,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.disaggregation.transport.engine import (
+    BaseTransferEngine,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.disaggregation.transport.manager import (
+    DiffusionTransferManager,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestTransferStaging(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        empty = torch.empty
+
+        def unpinned_empty(*args, **kwargs):
+            # CPU-only PyTorch has no pinned allocator. Keep the real pool
+            # storage, buddy allocator, tensor copies, and manifest IO.
+            kwargs.pop("pin_memory", None)
+            return empty(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        for scope in (
+            patch.object(torch, "empty", side_effect=unpinned_empty),
+            patch.object(torch, "get_device_module", return_value=torch.cpu),
+            patch.object(torch.cpu, "is_available", return_value=False),
+        ):
+            scope.start()
+            self.addCleanup(scope.stop)
+
+    def assert_staging_round_trip(
+        self, fields, offsets, slot_size, min_block_size=1 << 20
+    ):
+        buffer = TransferTensorBuffer(pool_size=2 << 20, min_block_size=min_block_size)
+        manager = DiffusionTransferManager(Mock(spec=BaseTransferEngine), buffer)
+        staged, event = manager.stage_tensors_async("request", fields, {"step": 1})
+        self.assertIsNotNone(staged)
+        self.assertIsNone(event)
+        self.assertEqual(staged.scalar_fields, {"step": 1})
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {
+                name: [entry["offset"] for entry in entries]
+                for name, entries in staged.manifest.items()
+            },
+            offsets,
+        )
+        if slot_size is None:
+            self.assertIsNone(staged.slot)
+        else:
+            self.assertEqual(staged.slot.size, slot_size)
+            restored = buffer.read_tensors_from_manifest(staged.slot, staged.manifest)
+            for name, value in fields.items():
+                if value is None or (isinstance(value, list) and not value):
+                    self.assertNotIn(name, restored)
+                else:
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(restored[name], value, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            if "parts" in staged.manifest:
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    [entry["list_index"] for entry in staged.manifest["parts"]],
+                    [i for i, value in enumerate(fields["parts"]) if value is not None],
+                )
+        manager.free_staged("request")
+        # The full pool must be reusable after staging cleanup.
+        whole_pool = buffer.allocate(buffer.pool_size, "next-request")
+        self.assertIsNotNone(whole_pool)
+        self.assertTrue(buffer.free(whole_pool))
+
+    def test_alignment_crosses_default_block_boundary(self):
+        """Raw bytes fit 1 MiB, but alignment pushes the second tensor past its slot."""
+        self.assert_staging_round_trip(
+            {
+                "first": torch.full((1_048_065,), 17, dtype=torch.uint8),
+                "second": torch.full((511,), 29, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            },
+            {"first": [0], "second": [1_048_576]},
+            2 << 20,
+        )
+
+    def test_list_holes_preserve_indices_and_alignment(self):
+        """Skipped entries must not break sizing or shift decoded list indices."""
+        self.assert_staging_round_trip(
+            {
+                "absent": None,
+                "empty": [],
+                "parts": [None, torch.arange(3), None, torch.arange(2)],
+                "tail": torch.tensor([7], dtype=torch.uint8),
+            },
+            {"parts": [0, 512], "tail": [1024]},
+            2048,
+            min_block_size=512,
+        )
+
+    def test_alignment_boundaries(self):
+        """Exercise both sides of 512B, aligned tensors, and a zero-length tail."""
+        for sizes, offsets, slot_size, minimum in (
+            ((511, 512), [0, 512], 1024, 512),
+            ((512, 512), [0, 512], 1024, 512),
+            ((513, 1), [0, 1024], 2048, 512),
+            ((3,), [0], 1 << 20, 1 << 20),
+            ((1, 0), [0, 512], 512, 1),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(sizes=sizes):
+                self.assert_staging_round_trip(
+                    {"parts": [torch.ones(size, dtype=torch.uint8) for size in sizes]},
+                    {"parts": offsets},
+                    slot_size,
+                    min_block_size=minimum,
+                )
+
+    def test_absent_fields_need_no_slot(self):
+        """Absent tensors and all-None lists stage only scalar metadata."""
+        for fields in ({"absent": None, "empty": []}, {"parts": [None, None]}):
+            with self.subTest(fields=fields):
+                self.assert_staging_round_trip(fields, {}, None)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
